_: THE ZONE CONTRACT. This file is the whole specification. Nothing in this pack types a track width, a percentage or a breakpoint: every width in every image is COMPUTED from the region contracts below, and every responsive threshold is a SUM of two minimums and a gap. `scripts/mockups-compositions.mjs` generates the layout CSS and the state queries from this file and then MEASURES the rendered result back against it, so an image that disagreed with the contract could not be produced.

base._note: The app sets no root font-size, so 1rem = 16px. Region minimums are stated in rem because they are reading measures, not device measures.

gap._note: One gap between any two tracks, in every primitive.

prompt.role: the question. A compact reading rail: it wants enough width to set a question without hyphenation and no more.
prompt.note: A TRACK IS A POSITION. No fill, no border, no stretching to the sibling's height.

solution.role: the numbered reasoning and the answer that closes it. Receives most of the surplus because reasoning lines are longer than question lines and mathematics does not wrap gracefully.
solution.note: The measure caps the PROSE inside the track, never the track. Surplus width the prose does not use stays unused.

case.role: one complete case in a comparison — its own question, reasoning and answer, stacked.
case.note: Equal grow: repeated children are identical by construction, so a comparison cannot develop a favoured side.

figure.role: a coordinate plane, geometric construction or table produced by the Figure Engine.
figure.note: CONTENT-SIZED, never fr-sized. Its width is whatever preserving its intrinsic aspect at a legible scale requires, bounded on the longer side at `bound` and floored at minW x minH. Below the floor the containing split is not viable and the composition changes state. minW/minH/bound are px because they are the engine's own legibility floor (MX_PLOT_MIN_W, MX_PLOT_MIN_H, MX_PLOT_H), not reading measures.

interpretation.role: what the figure shows and why it agrees with the working — the rail that belongs to a shared visual.
interpretation.note: MAINTAINER RULING WANTED: you suggested a 45-55rem maximum. The app currently caps this at MX_INTERP_MAX = 620px (38.75rem). The pack uses 40rem = 640px, the nearest round value to what ships; raise it to 48rem if the wider measure is what you want.

synthesis.role: the same semantic region as `interpretation`, in its other placement.
synthesis.note: ONE REGION, ONE STYLING CONTRACT, TWO PLACEMENTS. Beside a shared visual it is the interpretation rail; with no visual to belong to it spans the content region after the composition. `WHAT THIS SHOWS`, `WHY THE TWO AGREE` and `WHY IT AGREES` were three footer inventions for one thing; they are now one region whose placement is chosen by the primitive it lands in, and whose JSON key names that placement.

answer.role: the closing band of the solution it belongs to.
answer.note: INHERITED GEOMETRY. The answer has no width of its own: it begins at its owning solution's content origin and flows as text. It is never a card, never centred, never independently placed.

instructionSplit.purpose: an ordinary worked example: the question locates left, the reasoning runs right.

repeat.purpose: several instances of one child. `down` is a sequence of examples; `across` is a comparison of cases.
repeat.note: ITEM COUNT HAS NO EFFECT ON GEOMETRY. Two, three, five or ten children are the same child repeated. This is what permanently removes the 2 + 1 layout: there is no arrangement for a count to select.
repeat.fallback: across becomes down when the children cannot clear their minimums

visualInterpretation.purpose: a figure and the text that reads it, as siblings with one top edge.
visualInterpretation.note: The figure track is content-sized and the interpretation track takes the remainder, so there is no unclaimed space beside the plane. This is what the old `SHARED VISUAL at full width` lacked: an answer to what the rest of the row is for.

stack.purpose: the regions in semantic order, one inset, no divider, nothing centred.
stack.note: The terminal state. Every split falls back to it and it never fails: a region that cannot clear its minimum beside a sibling can always have the content region to itself.

visualCheck.assembly: state 1: instructionSplit(prompt, solution) | state 2: visualInterpretation(visual, interpretation)

extended.assembly: states; each state assembled from the primitives its own content needs

resolver: 1  Identify the semantic composition from the JSON. Never infer it from content.
2  Ask every region for its minimum, its growth weight, its reading measure, and — if it is a visual — its intrinsic aspect and minimum legible scale.

4  If every region clears its minimum, use it. Distribute the content region across the tracks by growth weight; a track that would fall below its minimum is frozen at its minimum and the remainder redistributed.
5  Otherwise try the next state, if the composition has one.
7  Content may increase height without limit.
8  Never reach a state by distorting a figure, narrowing prose below its minimum, centring orphan content, changing geometry with item count, or stretching an empty rail for balance.

surfaces._note: CONTENT REGION widths, not viewport widths. 1152 is a 1536px viewport with the navigation rail open; 382 is a 414px handset. 700 is not a chosen design width — it is a width that sits ABOVE the repeat-across floor and BELOW the visualInterpretation floor, so it renders whatever the grammar produces there. The pack shows it precisely because nobody designed it.
